title: Learning the ARTS of Search for Automated Discovery
abstract: arXiv:2606.21891v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Scientific discovery can be formulated as an iterative search process over the space of hypotheses and experiments. Contemporary methods navigate this space using heuristics such as MCTS. These algorithms conflate the merit of a hypothesis with the quality of its experimental execution. A promising hypothesis with preliminary execution is therefore ranked below a modest hypothesis whose execution is refined. Moreover, prior methods prune the search logs as the search progresses because the accumulated history outgrows the context window. We propose Agentic Reasoning for Tree Search (ARTS), where we deploy a reasoning language model to navigate this space. The model inspects prior execution logs, diagnoses whether earlier failures arose from faulty implementations or bad hypotheses, and selects the hypothesis to build on next. translated_title: 学习搜索的艺术以促进自动发现
translated_abstract: 科学发现可以被表述为在假设和实验空间中的迭代搜索过程。当代方法使用诸如蒙特卡洛树搜索（MCTS）等启发式算法来导航这一空间。这些算法将假设的价值与其实验执行的质量混为一谈。因此，一个具有初步执行的有前景的假设会被排在一个执行精良但普通的假设之下。此外，先前的方法在搜索过程中会修剪搜索日志，因为累积的历史记录超出了上下文窗口。我们提出了基于代理推理的树搜索（ARTS），其中我们部署了一个推理语言模型来导航这一空间。该模型检查先前的执行日志，诊断早期失败是源于错误实现还是糟糕的假设，并选择下一个要构建的假设。为了缓解上下文长度的挑战，ARTS使用测试时训练来灌输搜索的知识。
tldr: 提出了ARTS方法，通过推理语言模型和测试时训练，区分假设价值与执行质量，并解决搜索日志上下文长度问题，从而提升自动科学发现的效率。
en_tdlr: ARTS is proposed to enhance automated scientific discovery by using a reasoning language model and test-time training to separate hypothesis merit from execution quality and address context length issues in search logs.
